f.title: Consider vaccine epidemiological impact and individual protection in benefit-risk
f.statement: For vaccines already in the extended vaccination programme, the impact of the vaccine on the epidemiology of the vaccine-preventable condition should be considered as well as the impact on individual protection; the risk-benefit balance may change in later programme stages (herd immunity), and differences in morbidity and mortality of the infectious disease between countries have to be considered.

f.title: Make public communication a collaborative undertaking
f.statement: Delivery of rapid, transparent, accurate and well-balanced information on the scientific evidence base is warranted; communication to the public should be a collaborative undertaking between industry, regulators and public health organisations with input from all stakeholders, clearly explaining what is known about the safety and efficacy of a vaccine when first used and what processes are in place to gather additional safety data.
